parsed.explanation: In Claim 3.2 the text takes an arbitrary minimal transversal T of C and immediately writes π(T)=∏_{p∈T}p, which is defined only for finite T; nothing in the text shows minimal transversals of C are finite (finiteness of members of C does not give it, as the objector's family {{x,t_n}} illustrates: an intersecting antichain of finite sets with an infinite minimal transversal). So Claim 3.2 is proved only for finite minimal transversals. This matters: in Step 4 hypothesis (iii) is invoked twice — in Case A on T⊆I∪Z_s (finite, harmless), but in the closing paragraph on a minimal transversal T⊆I∪Z_ω, an infinite set, where finiteness of T is deduced only from T∈C. Hence the final contradiction rests on (iii) for a possibly infinite T, which Step 3 has not established. The gap is not repaired elsewhere.
